title: Information Revelation and Alignment Faking in Stochastic Differential Games
summary: In competitive games with private objectives, actions can reveal information about hidden parameters. However, quantifying such information revelation is nontrivial, since it depends not only on the opponent's hidden parameter but also on the opponent's model of the game. We study this problem via a two-player linear-quadratic stochastic differential game under partial information, in which each player knows its own coupling parameter and models the opponent's hidden parameter through a prior.
